question: Can a passive three-loop dump network that damps differential circuit-current modes more strongly than the common mode reduce both transient magnetic-shape and distributed-force departure by at least 1.5 times relative to the fixed independent-dump control, without increasing the normalized current-squared-time or peak modeled resistive-element voltage proxies by more than five percent?
assumptions: The three winding circuits use the CASE-007 fault-balanced partition of the 18 public SIMSOPT NCSX modular coils. This is a hypothetical new-design topology, not a reconstruction or retrofit prescription for the historical NCSX electrical system.

The circuit inductance matrix is calculated from a midpoint Neumann integral with a fixed 20 mm distance regularization and continuous turn-count scaling inherited from CASE-007, then normalized by mean circuit self-inductance. It is a geometry-coupled dimensionless surrogate, not a winding-pack inductance calculation.

After a fault starts, the power supply contributes no voltage. One circuit receives a prescribed dimensionless quench resistance that rises linearly to three by normalized time 0.4. The protection network activates at time 0.12 and the ODE L dx/dt + (R_protection + R_quench) x = 0 is integrated to time 10.

The independent-dump control has three private unit resistors and no pair-shared branches. A candidate has three equal private resistors p and three equal pair-shared resistors b = p(rho - 1)/3, giving common-mode resistance p and two differential-mode resistances p rho. Only passive candidates with p in [0.25, 2] and rho in [1, 4] are accepted.

Magnetic-shape departure removes the best common current scale. Force-shape departure removes the corresponding common-current-squared force pattern. Both reuse the CASE-007 filament and plasma-surface proxies and are evaluated over each of the three possible initiating circuits.

The current-squared-time metric is normalized to the control and is not converted to conductor temperature. The voltage metric is the largest normalized drop across a modeled quench, private, or shared resistive element and is not a terminal-to-ground, turn-to-turn, insulation, switch, diode, or power-supply voltage.
The reference and fine coil meshes use 128 and 256 segments. The fine transient is repeated at half the time step. These checks measure only declared numerical stability.

The model, thresholds, and candidate settings were selected during interactive feasibility exploration before the formal Core lineage was recorded. This is exploratory mechanism evidence, not preregistered confirmation.

Passing justifies a higher-fidelity conductor, switching, dimensional voltage, thermal, structural, and plasma-response study. It does not establish a practical protection system, safety, novelty, patentability, or commercial value.

requirements.statement: The fine-mesh candidate reduces the worst transient magnetic-shape departure by at least 1.5 times relative to the fixed independent-dump control.
The fine-mesh candidate reduces the worst transient distributed-force-shape departure by at least 1.5 times relative to the fixed independent-dump control.
The worst normalized initiating-circuit current-squared-time proxy is no more than 1.05 times the fixed independent-dump control.
The worst modeled normalized resistive-element voltage is no more than 1.05 times the fixed independent-dump control.
The candidate leaves no more than one-millionth of its initial normalized magnetic energy at the end of the simulated interval.
The largest relative change in a primary candidate/control metric between reference and fine coil meshes is no more than one percent.
The largest relative change in a primary fine-mesh metric when the time step is halved is no more than one tenth of one percent.
The fine normalized circuit inductance matrix has condition number no greater than two.
The relative spread among the three initiating-circuit cases is no greater than one-billionth for every primary fine-mesh fault metric.

categorical_requirements.statement: The candidate lies inside the declared box and maps to nonnegative private and pair-shared passive resistances.
